newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico petchem industry seen growing through 2010.
newsitem.headline: Mexico petchem industry seen growing through 2010.

text.p: A private think-tank has predicted petrochemicals output will jump by more than five percent on average per year through 2010 after a 1.16 percent decline in 1996, the group said in a report obtained by Reuters on Wednesday.
The National Manufacturing Industry Chamber's Economic Studies Center estimated installed capacity would grow an average 5.4 percent over the same 13-year period.

Mexico should be a net exporter of petrochemicals by 2006, after at least ten years of trade deficits, according to the report. In 1996, the country's petrochemical trade deficit totalled $1.163 billion.

The government is revamping the industry with a sell-off of 49 percent of the nation's 10 principal plants of feedstock, currently owned by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex). Industry observers expect the move to rejuvenate the sector.
